review_notes:
I read all four theorems in the file (lines 1–118) and the declarations they depend on: exists_remote_scaling_sequence, exists_remote_scaling_conjugations, scaling_vector_limit, remoteCopy_commutator_tendsto, remoteCopy_conjugation_tendsto, scaling_defect_tendsto_of_cyclic, rightAction_adjoint_defect(_tendsto), exists_coisometry_graph_shift, exists_isometry_graph_shift, ModularConjugationData and tomitaPolarConjugation. I also read the parallel file SpatialModularCoisometries.lean.

Other options I considered and rejected:
- Weakening `t < 1` to `t ≤ 1`. The case t = 1 holds trivially with v = 1, so this needs a separate argument for no real gain.
- Weakening `hd` so the conjugations only have to agree on the vectors `M Ω`. Both maps are continuous and `M Ω` is dense (S.cyclic), so this condition is equivalent to `hd`, not weaker.
- Removing `hd` altogether through a uniqueness theorem for the modular conjugation. I found no such theorem, and removing a hypothesis belongs to a different rubric anyway.
- Generalising `exists_modular_graph_shift_adjoint` in the same way. That would need a version of `rightAction_adjoint_defect` for vectors other than Ω. It is mathematically routine but not available in the library, so I only mention it in the finding.

Uncertainty: I could not compile anything. The proposed proof only reuses the existing `choose`/`remoteCopy` construction and lemma calls that already appear in the cited files. Nothing in the repository uses these theorems yet, so the benefit is to future users.

findings.problem:
The file proves two separate facts about the same sequence `S.remoteCopy n (w n)`:
- `exists_modular_coisometry_sequence` gives conjugation convergence but only gives the scaling defect at the base vector Ω.
- `exists_modular_scaling_all_vectors` gives the defect at every vector but drops conjugation convergence.

As a result, `exists_modular_graph_shift` can only use the general lemma `exists_coisometry_graph_shift`, which accepts any pair `(ξ η : H)`, with η fixed to Ω (`... hconv ξ Ω (t : ℂ) hscale ...`). The graph-shift statement is therefore needlessly limited to vectors of the form `y.val Ω`, even though the underlying lemma and the construction both support any η.
findings.proposed_change:
1. Combine the two sequence theorems into one, the same way `exists_spatial_modular_coisometries` does in the spatial file:
```
theorem exists_modular_coisometry_sequence (J : H ≃ₗᵢ⋆[ℂ] H) (d : ModularConjugationData M Ω)
    (hd : d.conjugation = tomitaPolarConjugation J Ω S.separating S.cyclic)
    {t : ℝ} (ht : 0 < t) (ht1 : t < 1) :
    ∃ v : ℕ → Algebra M, (∀ n, v n*star (v n)=1) ∧
      (∀ ξ : H, Tendsto (fun n => (v n).val ξ-(t : ℂ) • d.rightAction (v n) ξ) atTop (𝓝 0)) ∧
      (∀ (a : Algebra M) (η : H),
        Tendsto (fun n => (v n*a*star (v n)).val η) atTop (𝓝 (a.val η)))
```
Proof sketch: run the `choose s w … using fun n => S.exists_scaling_coisometry_near hr hr1 …` construction from `exists_remote_scaling_conjugations`. Then:
- Get conjugation convergence from `S.remoteCopy_conjugation_tendsto d s w hco hscale hc hc1 hcr`.
- Get commutator convergence from `S.remoteCopy_commutator_tendsto s w hco hscale (fun n => (hlt n).le)`. This is exactly what `exists_remote_scaling_sequence` uses for the same sequence.
- Get the defect at Ω from `scaling_vector_limit` as now, then extend it to every ξ with `d.scaling_defect_tendsto_of_cyclic S.cyclic`, as lines 47–56 already do.

2. Restate the graph shift for an arbitrary pair of vectors:
```
theorem exists_modular_graph_shift … (ξ η : H) … :
    ∃ y : Algebra M,
      ‖y.val η-d.rightAction y ξ‖ < ‖(t : ℂ) • x.val η-d.rightAction x ξ‖+ε ∧ …
```
with proof `obtain ⟨v,hv,hall,hconv⟩ := …; exact d.exists_coisometry_graph_shift v hv hconv ξ η (t : ℂ) (hall η) x F hε`. Setting η := Ω recovers the current statement.
findings.benefit: Users get one sequence with both properties instead of two incompatible existential statements. The graph-shift result then matches the generality of `exists_coisometry_graph_shift`, so it applies to any vector, not just Ω. It also brings the remote file into line with its spatial counterpart, which already returns both properties for a single sequence.
